entities.name: An-Nasir Ahmad
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
An-Nasir Ahmad, who reigned as the third imam of the Zaidi state in Yemen from 913 CE until his death in 937 CE, stands as a pivotal figure in the consolidation and expansion of this distinct Shi'a polity in the Arabian Peninsula. Born Ahmad ibn Yahya, he inherited the nascent imamate from his father, Al-Hadi ila'l-Haqq Yahya, and his brother, Muhammad, transforming a localized religious movement into a formidable political and military power. His reign marked a critical period for the Zaidi Imamate, establishing a foundational legal and administrative framework that would influence Yemeni history for centuries.

During his 24-year rule, An-Nasir Ahmad engaged in extensive military campaigns, notably against the rival Isma'ili Qarmatians who challenged Zaidi authority in the northern highlands and Tihama coastal plain. He successfully repelled Qarmatian incursions, securing the Zaidi heartland around Sa'ada and Sana'a. Beyond military prowess, An-Nasir Ahmad was a prolific scholar and jurist, contributing significantly to Zaidi jurisprudence and theology. He authored numerous works on Islamic law (fiqh) and hadith, solidifying the Zaidi school of thought and ensuring its intellectual vitality, which complemented his political efforts to stabilize the state.
